title: HyAtten: Hybrid Photonic-Digital Architecture for Accelerating Attention Mechanism
problem: Photonic accelerators for attention mechanisms suffer from high signal conversion overhead (ADC/DAC latency), limiting practical speedup despite the intrinsic speed and energy advantages of photonics.
motivation: Transformers demand massive computational resources; photonic computing offers high energy efficiency and speed, but signal conversion overhead negates these benefits in practical deployments.
method: The system uses a signal comparator (a circuit that examines incoming data) to split the work between two paths. Low-precision signals use low-resolution photonic converters, which can process many operations in parallel through photonic circuits. High-precision signals bypass the slow conversion step and go straight to digital circuits instead. By routing each type of signal to the right processor, the system avoids the expensive conversion overhead that normally limits photonic speedup.
key_novelty: The core innovation is choosing where each signal gets processed—photonic converters for low-precision data, digital circuits for high-precision data—so the expensive signal conversion only happens when photonic processing can actually speed things up.
contributions: 9.8x performance/area improvement over state-of-the-art photonic transformer accelerator
2.2x energy-efficiency/area improvement over prior photonic approaches
Signal classification and hybrid processing strategy
limitations: Evaluation compared to photonic systems only; comparison to digital transformers and hybrid CPU/GPU systems not discussed.
primary_theme: hybrid photonic-digital attention accelerator with adaptive signal routing
